shipments.title: Iron ore shipments
shipments.content:
Shipments are iron ore tonnes (wet basis, Mt) sold and delivered in the period -- the volume half of the revenue equation.

For Fortescue: shipments have plateaued around 190-200 Mtpa since FY2023 as the Pilbara hub network matured; further revenue growth now depends mostly on price and product mix (Fortescue Metals vs the higher-grade Iron Bridge magnetite), not volume.

What to watch:

  • Full-year guidance vs actual shipments
  • Cyclone/weather disruptions to the H1 half
  • Iron Bridge magnetite ramp adding a second, higher-price product

priceCost.title: Realised price vs C1 cash cost
priceCost.content:
Realised price is the average US$ received per dry tonne (dmt) of ore sold, net of the quality/grade discount Fortescue's lower-grade ore attracts against the benchmark 62% Fe index. C1 cost is the cash cost to mine, process and ship a wet tonne (wmt) -- it excludes royalties, depreciation and capital.

For Fortescue: this spread is the single biggest swing factor in earnings -- the realised price moves with the benchmark iron ore price (largely set by Chinese steel demand) while C1 cost is comparatively sticky, so a falling iron ore price compresses margin dollar-for-dollar much faster than costs can be cut.

What to watch:

  • Realised price as a % of the 62% Fe benchmark (the grade discount)
  • C1 cost creep from strip ratio increases as pits deepen
  • Both figures are annual-only -- Fortescue's half-year releases report a different cost basis that isn't directly comparable

underlyingEbitda.title: Underlying EBITDA
underlyingEbitda.content:
Underlying EBITDA is Fortescue's own non-IFRS earnings measure, excluding significant items (impairments, disposals, one-off restructuring) that distort statutory EBITDA in a given period.

For Fortescue: management and the market anchor guidance and consensus on this line rather than statutory EBITDA -- it is also the number that maps most directly onto the price/cost/volume drivers above.

What to watch:

  • Underlying EBITDA margin versus the realised price cycle
  • Gap to statutory EBITDA (size of excluded items)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Fortescue: equity growth has been driven by retained earnings through the iron ore up-cycle rather than share issuance -- watch whether it holds up as Fortescue Energy's green hydrogen/metals capex ramps.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Energy-transition capex commitments not yet on the balance sheet

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Fortescue: net debt is low relative to peak-cycle EBITDA, giving balance-sheet room to keep funding the Energy division's growth capex through an iron ore price downturn.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus mid-cycle (not peak) EBITDA
  • Energy division capex draw-down on committed facilities

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Fortescue: statutory EBITDA swings with significant items; the Underlying EBITDA chart above strips those out and is the more comparable series year to year.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend across the iron ore price cycle
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Fortescue: the payout ratio typically tracks 65-80% of underlying NPAT -- dividends move directly with the iron ore price cycle rather than being smoothed.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividend cuts in a falling-price year versus funding from debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Fortescue: FCF is highly cyclical with the iron ore price and Energy division capex, so the DCF is built on a mid-cycle owner-FCF, not the latest year's actual.

What to watch:

  • FCF trough years versus the mid-cycle assumption in the DCF
  • Energy division capex crowding out shareholder distributions

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Fortescue: all three margins compress and expand almost entirely with the realised iron ore price -- cost side moves are second-order by comparison.

What to watch:

  • Margin trend across a full price cycle, not one year
  • One-offs (impairments) distorting net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Fortescue: CapEx includes both stay-in-business Pilbara sustaining spend and growth capital for the Energy division (hydrogen, green metals) -- the DCF splits these where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • Energy division capex rising as a share of total CapEx
  • OCF that diverges from Underlying EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Fortescue: the three lines together show how much of an iron-ore price move flows straight through to the bottom line.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for iron ore shipped in the period, before any costs.

For Fortescue: revenue is realised price times shipments (see the Iron Ore Operating Drivers section) -- the YoY swing is dominated by the benchmark iron ore price, not volume, since shipments have plateaued.

What to watch:

  • Whether a revenue move is a price or volume story
  • Interim rows show cyclone-season seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Fortescue: the share count has been broadly flat -- the DCF holds it constant and charges SBC as a cash cost, which this chart is the check on.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising unexpectedly
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
